issue.title: Feature: pip package for SDK
issue.body: Status: @JonasVautherin currently working on windows support

comments.body: ➤ Jonas Vautherin commented: In order to get the "manylinux1 compatibility label" when distributing on pip, one needs to build with... manylinux1... which is based on CentOS 5, which is old. We depend on BoringSSL, which required Go to build, which cannot be installed on CentOS 5. Julian Oes mentioned [PEP 513](https://www.python.org/dev/peps/pep-0513/#the-manylinux1-policy) which mentions libcrypt.so as a possible dynamic library, but that's not what we need. We need libcrypto.so, libcrypt.so coming from glibc (as far as I understand). So I went for OpenSSL. OpenSSL requires Perl 5.10 to build, and CentOS 5 has Perl 5.8.8. After a while, I found a way to customize our manylinux1 cross-compiler to build its own more recent version of Perl. Then I realized that CentOS 5 depends on libc 2.5. And gRPC uses some stuff that comes from libc 2.6 (and that is not compatible with musl, btw). So I hardcoded a way to use the musl-compatible alternative (I'll check with the gRPC maintainer to get a clean fix for that later). After all that, it appears that gRPC relies on CMAKE_CROSSCOMPILATION, which is (in my understanding) a bad idea. It took me a while to figure that out, and finally, I just managed to build gRPC with manylinux (at least it seems so, the installation step actually failed for a permission issue). Not looking too bad overall, but it is not straightforward to distribute C++ in pip, as we could have expected.

➤ Thomas Gubler commented:

Status:
all dependencies compiled with manylinux
cross compiling grpc is not used a lot by other people, Jonas had to find to workaround; he is bringing those upstream

next step:
get grpc to work fully

➤ Thomas Gubler commented:

status:
grpc PR accepted
build dependencies aginst manylinux
trying to build sdk against those dependencies
Just got to build `backend_bin` with `manylinux1`. May have a PoC soon!

➤ Thomas Gubler commented:

Status:
grpc server running on windows and in CI;
naming dicussion resolved (allows to make package for linux an MacOS)

➤ Thomas Gubler commented:

Status:
Cmake for C++ backend PR almost ready to merge
allows pip packages for Linux, MacOS and partially Windows --> allow manual release of pip packages for Linux and MacOS

Next Steps:
integrate into CI
upstream grpc changes

➤ Julian Oes commented:

Status by Jonas: Manylinux build generated in CI. Next step is to release backend artefact to use in langage wrappers such as Python using pip.

We have the first package out on pip: `pip3 install mavsdk` works on macOS, Linux and Windows.

The release process is currently quite manual, but good enough to close this issue. More automation will come later.
